features.text: Patient is 39 years old and female.
Patient has been experiencing uncontrolled blood pressure, especially around the time of hospital admission.
Patient has had headaches, vomiting, and lightheadedness associated with high blood pressure.
Patient experienced vomiting and constipation prior to hospital admission, which improved after a bowel movement.
Patient does not have a family history of hypertension or cardiovascular conditions.
Patient does not have a history of dizziness or vision changes with headaches, but experienced lightheadedness related to blood pressure.
Patient has quadriplegia from a spinal cord injury and uses a supra-pubic catheter.
Patient manages constipation with Miralax and lactulose when needed.
Patient does not have significant previous illnesses, surgeries, or allergies.
Patient has experienced spasms related to quadriplegia, but not connected to headaches or vomiting.
Patient's blood pressure was high and fluctuating during hospital admission, but exact readings are not available.
Patient's headaches were intense and occurred with vomiting and lightheadedness, but not constant.
Patient did not notice any specific activities or times of day that worsened headaches.
Patient did not experience changes in vision, balance, or coordination during headache episodes.
Patient was told that neurological exams during hospital stay did not find any major abnormalities.
Patient did not experience changes in vision, balance, coordination, or limb weakness during hospital stay.
Patient did not receive specific details about reflexes, motor function, or sensory testing from neurological exams.
